use_case_name: Browse and Search Files and Archives

claims.content: Allow the user to browse and gain access to every area of the computer system (e.g. storing units, desktop, users documents etc) as well as to included objects (archives and files), including searching within folders and subfolders.

goal.raw_text: Allow the user to browse and gain access to every area of the computer system (e.g. storing units, desktop, users documents etc) as well as to included objects (archives and files), including searching within folders and subfolders.

claims.content: User
The PeaZip application is installed on the computer system.
An operating system is present on the computer system.
The user has access to the File Manager Interface.
The user presses the 'File' button in the initial window (file manager interface) to open a submenu with choices for browsing and accessing areas and objects of the computer systems.

trigger.raw_text: The user presses the 'File' button in the initial window (file manager interface) to open a submenu with choices for browsing and accessing areas and objects of the computer systems.

claims.content: The user selects 'Filesystem' from the File menu to access an object list organized according to a functional hierarchy.
The user browses and gains access to every area of the computer system (e.g., storing units, desktop, users documents) as well as included objects (archives and files).
The user utilizes navigation buttons (back, forward, up) and the refresh button in the navigation bar to navigate through the file manager interface.
To perform a search in this folder and subfolders, the user presses F3 or uses the recursive search function.
To perform a non-recursive search (search here), the user presses Ctrl+F3.
The user can toggle between browse mode and flat view mode using F6 or the '*' key.
The user can browse the desktop by pressing F2.
The user can browse the user's home directory by pressing Ctrl+F2.
The user can browse the computer's root directory by pressing Shift+F2.
If browsing inside an archive, the user can browse the archive root by pressing Ctrl+Shift+F2; otherwise, this action browses the computer's root.
The user can navigate up one level in the directory structure by pressing F4.
The user can refresh the currently displayed content by pressing F5.
The user can browse the most recently visited item by pressing F7 (or using Ctrl, second, Shift, third modifiers).
The user can browse the first item in the bookmarks list by pressing F8 (or using Ctrl, second, Shift, third modifiers).
The user can go directly to the computer system's or archive's root by pressing Ctrl+R.
If a function is format-specific and not supported for the current archive type, it will be ignored.
The user has successfully gained access to the desired area of the computer system or included object (archive/file).
The file manager interface displays the contents of the selected location or archive.
If a search was performed, the interface displays the results matching the search criteria within the specified scope (folder and subfolders or current folder only).
